summary: Wen-ling Jane works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied under Lobsang Jamspal and earned her PhD at Columbia University, where she was supervised by Robert A. F. Thurman (attested 2009).

Wenbiao Mai specializes in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Kyoto University, the University of Hamburg, and Peking University, where he earned a PhD, and served as a visiting assistant professor at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2013).

Wendi L. Adamek specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She studied under Michel Strickmann, Seizan Yanagida, and Hidehiko Koga, completing her PhD at Stanford University in 1998, and held posts at Barnard College (attested 2008) and the University of Calgary (attested 2018–2026).

Wendy Doniger is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. She earned an MA and PhD at Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls, and a D.Phil. at Oxford under Robert Charles Zaehner, joining the University of Chicago faculty in 1978.
Wendy Palace specializes in history, archaeology, and Tibetology. She completed her PhD at Durham University under the supervision of David Sweet.
Wenjiang Ding (1887–1936) was a scholar of history and archaeology. He studied under Qichao Liang, attended Peking University, and later held a post at Peking University from around 1931 to 1934.

Wenjie Duan (1917–2011) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at the Sichuan Fine Arts Institute and Central Academy of Fine Arts, he held multiple leadership posts at Dunhuang Academy between 1946 and 1998.

Wenjie Qin works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. She completed her PhD at Harvard University under doctoral supervisor Wei-ming Tu and studied with Diana L. Eck, Masatoshi Nagatomi, Charles Hallisey, and Robert M. Gimello.

Werner Abraham (1936–2024) was a linguist who earned his PhD at the University of Vienna. He held positions at the universities of Illinois, Tübingen, and Munich, and was a professor of medieval studies and German linguistics at Groningen from 1971.

Werner Sundermann (1935–2012) was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held academic posts at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1967–1970), the Academy of Sciences of the GDR (~1970–1991), and the Free University of Berlin (~1993–2000).
Wes Borton specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at East Carolina University under Derek F. Maher and pursued studies at the University of Michigan (attested 2010).

Whalen Lai is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He studied at International Christian University and earned a PhD from Harvard University (~1969–1975), later teaching at the University of Illinois (~1976–1978) and UC Davis (~1978–2007).

Whitney Cox specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Virginia and the University of Chicago, learning under Wendy Doniger and Sheldon Pollock, and later became a professor at the University of Chicago (~2012).

Wijesinghe Sugathadasa Karunaratne (1928–1986) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at the University of Ceylon and SOAS University of London (PhD), later teaching at the University of Ceylon and the University of Kelaniya.

Wilburn Hansen is a scholar of Japanology and religious studies. He pursued a master's program at the University of Colorado Boulder and studied at Stanford University under Bernard Faure and Carl Bielefeldt.

Wilfred Cantwell Smith (1916–2000) was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who earned his PhD at Princeton. He held major posts at Forman Christian College, McGill University, Dalhousie University, and Harvard University.

Wilfrid Sellars (1912–1989) was a philosopher educated at Michigan, Buffalo, and Oxford. He taught at the universities of Iowa, Minnesota, and Yale before holding a professorship at the University of Pittsburgh from 1963 to 1989.

Wilhelm Deecke (1831–1897) was a linguist and Indologist. He earned his doctorate at the University of Leipzig, studied in Berlin under scholars including Albrecht Weber and Franz Bopp, and later served as director at schools in Lübeck, Bouxwiller, and Mulhouse.

Wilhelm Dilthey (1833–1911) was a philosopher who studied at Heidelberg University and Humboldt University of Berlin. He held posts at the University of Basel (~1866–1868), Kiel University (~1868–1871), the University of Breslau (~1871–1882), and Humboldt University (~1882–1905).

Wilhelm Geiger (1856–1943) was an Indologist and Iranian studies scholar. He completed his PhD and Habilitation under Friedrich von Spiegel at Erlangen-Nuremberg, where he became a professor in 1891, before serving as a professor at Munich (1920–1924).
